learn.title: Green Steel Revolution
learn.intro: Green steel production replaces coal with hydrogen in blast furnaces, cutting CO2 emissions by up to 90%. This tech is vital for decarbonizing industry, a major emissions source. India's steel sector could save 500 million tons of CO2 annually by adopting this method.
learn.c1_text: Hydrogen replaces coal in blast furnaces, producing steel without carbon emissions. Like swapping gasoline for electric in cars, it eliminates the dirty fuel. A single ton of green steel saves 2 tons of CO2. Australia's Hybrit plant produces 10,000 tons monthly using this method.
learn.c2_text: Green hydrogen is produced via electrolysis using renewable energy. It requires massive clean power, like India's 140 GW solar farms. Costs are dropping; electrolysis now costs $2-3/kg vs $6/kg for gray hydrogen. India aims for 5 million tons/year green steel by 2030.
learn.c3_text: India's National Hydrogen Mission targets 5 GW hydrogen production by 2030. Tata Steel is testing hydrogen blast furnaces in Odisha. The government offers 30% tax incentives for green steel plants. This could make India a global leader in low-carbon steel.
learn.stat1: India's steel industry emits 800 million tons CO2 yearly (2023 data)
learn.stat2: Green hydrogen costs $3.5/kg in India (2024 estimate)
learn.stat3: Tata Steel's pilot plant aims for 100% green steel by 2028
learn.stat4: India's steel demand to reach 200 million tons/year by 2030

learn.title: Capacity Factor Basics
learn.intro: Capacity factor shows how much energy a power plant actually produces vs its maximum potential. A solar farm with 25% capacity factor means it runs at full power only 25% of the time. This concept explains why renewables need backup power or storage.
learn.c1_text: Capacity factor = Actual output / Max possible output over time. A coal plant might have 85% (runs constantly), while solar averages 15-25% due to night and clouds. Like a factory that only operates during daylight hours.
learn.c2_text: A 100 MW solar plant with 20% capacity factor produces 350 GWh/year. Contrast with a 100 MW nuclear plant at 90% capacity factor (780 GWh). This gap requires grid flexibility, like India's 24/7 renewable energy policy requiring backup systems.
learn.c3_text: India's solar farms average 18% capacity factor due to monsoon rains. The government mandates 25% capacity factor for new solar projects. This drives innovation in energy storage, with 10 GW battery storage planned by 2025 to compensate for low capacity factors.
learn.stat2: Nuclear plants average 85% capacity factor in India
learn.stat3: Battery storage needed: 10 GW by 2025 to balance solar variability

learn.title: Solar PV Magic
learn.intro: Solar panels convert sunlight directly into electricity using the photoelectric effect. When photons hit silicon cells, they knock electrons loose, creating current. This clean energy source powers 30 million Indian homes today.
learn.c1_text: Photons from sunlight excite electrons in silicon cells, creating a current. Like a water wheel turning with flowing water, photons push electrons through a circuit. A 1 m² panel generates 200-300W under full sun.
learn.c2_text: The photoelectric effect requires semiconductor materials like silicon. When photons hit the material, they create electron-hole pairs that flow as current. This process is 15-22% efficient in commercial panels. India's solar farms use this principle to generate 70 GW capacity.
learn.c3_text: India added 16 GW solar in 2023, now 70 GW total. The government's 500 GW solar target by 2030 relies on this tech. Tamil Nadu's solar parks use this principle to power 2 million homes. Local manufacturing reduces costs to ₹2.44/kWh.
learn.stat3: Tamil Nadu solar parks power 2 million homes

learn.title: EV Power Secrets
learn.intro: Electric vehicles use motors to convert battery electricity into motion. Regenerative braking recovers energy during deceleration. India has 2 million EVs, with charging infrastructure growing 40% yearly.
learn.c1_text: EV motors turn electricity into mechanical energy, similar to how a fan motor spins. Lithium-ion batteries store energy like a fuel tank. A Tesla Model 3's 60 kWh battery provides 350 km range. India's EVs use similar tech but adapted for local conditions.
learn.c2_text: When braking, the motor acts as a generator, converting kinetic energy back to electricity. This can recover 15-20% of energy. Like braking a train to recharge batteries, it extends range. Indian EVs like Tata Nexon use this feature to improve efficiency on city roads.
learn.c3_text: India's EV market grew 80% in 2023, with 2 million vehicles. The Faster Adoption and Manufacturing (FAME) scheme supports charging infrastructure. Delhi has 500 public chargers. Local companies like Ola Electric are developing battery swapping stations using this technology.
learn.stat4: Ola Electric plans 10,000 battery swapping stations by 2025

learn.title: Wind Power Basics
learn.intro: Small wind turbines convert wind kinetic energy into electricity using rotor blades and generators. A 10 kW turbine can power a home. India has 40 MW small wind capacity, with potential to reach 100 MW by 2030.
learn.c1_text: Wind turns rotor blades, spinning a generator inside. Like a bicycle generator, this motion creates electricity. A 10 kW turbine needs 5 m/s wind speed. India's wind farms use this principle to generate 40 MW capacity.
learn.c2_text: The rotor's movement drives a generator via gears. Modern turbines use direct drive systems for reliability. They operate best at 12-25 m/s winds. Small turbines are ideal for Indian villages with average 6-8 m/s winds.
learn.c3_text: India's 40 MW small wind capacity powers 15,000 homes. The government targets 100 MW by 2030. Tamil Nadu and Gujarat lead with successful village installations. A 5 kW turbine costs ₹1.5 lakh, making it affordable for rural households.

learn.title: Microgrid Solutions
learn.intro: Microgrids are localized energy systems that can operate independently. They use renewables and storage to provide power during grid failures. India's microgrids serve 500 villages, enhancing disaster resilience and energy independence.
learn.c1_text: Microgrids connect solar/wind to batteries and controls. They operate like a village power plant. When main grid fails, they isolate and keep running. India's microgrids use this to keep lights on during monsoon storms.
learn.c2_text: They combine renewables with battery storage. During grid outages, they switch to island mode. This requires smart controllers. India's microgrids can power 500 villages, providing 24/7 power even during grid failures.
learn.c3_text: India's microgrids served 500 villages during 2023 floods. The government's Smart Villages Program deploys them in disaster-prone areas. A 100 kW microgrid costs ₹15 lakh, funded by state governments. They use local solar and batteries for resilience.
learn.stat4: Microgrids reduce blackouts by 40% in rural areas
